questions.q: Which club did Marco Reus join when he left Borussia Mönchengladbach in 2012?
questions.hint: Reus, the 2012 Bundesliga Player of the Year, returned to his boyhood club Borussia Dortmund in the summer of 2012.

questions.q: Marc-André ter Stegen left Gladbach in 2014 to join which club?
questions.hint: The academy-produced goalkeeper joined FC Barcelona in 2014, where he became first choice for years.

questions.q: Granit Xhaka was sold by Gladbach to which Premier League club in 2016?
questions.hint: Gladbach sold their Swiss midfield general to Arsenal in the summer of 2016.

questions.q: Which coach led Gladbach to a fourth-place Bundesliga finish in 2019-20 before later leaving for Borussia Dortmund?
questions.hint: Marco Rose took Gladbach to fourth and Champions League qualification in 2019-20, then moved to Dortmund in 2021.

questions.q: In the 2020-21 Champions League round of 16, Gladbach were knocked out by which club?
questions.hint: Gladbach's first-ever run to the Champions League knockout stage ended against Manchester City, who won both legs 2-0.

questions.q: Which team did Gladbach thrash 6-0 away in the 2020-21 Champions League group stage?
questions.hint: Gladbach won 6-0 away against Shakhtar Donetsk in November 2020, one of the biggest results in their European history.

questions.q: Marcus Thuram left Gladbach on a free transfer in 2023 to join which club?
questions.hint: Thuram ran down his contract and joined Inter Milan for free in the summer of 2023.

questions.q: From which French club did Gladbach sign striker Alassane Pléa in 2018?
questions.hint: Pléa arrived from OGC Nice in 2018 in a then club-record deal for Gladbach.

questions.q: Yann Sommer left Gladbach in January 2023 to join which club?
questions.hint: Sommer joined Bayern Munich in January 2023 as cover for the injured Manuel Neuer; his move to Inter came only later that year.

questions.q: Which club did Gladbach famously beat 5-0 in the DFB-Pokal in October 2021?
questions.hint: Gladbach humiliated holders Bayern Munich 5-0 in the second round of the 2021-22 DFB-Pokal.

questions.q: In the 2011 relegation playoff, Gladbach preserved their Bundesliga status against which club?
questions.hint: Under Lucien Favre, Gladbach beat VfL Bochum over two legs in the May 2011 relegation playoff to stay up.

questions.q: Which midfielder, then playing for Gladbach, started the 2014 World Cup final for Germany?
questions.hint: Christoph Kramer started the 2014 final against Argentina but was substituted early after a concussion.

questions.q: Who succeeded Max Eberl as Gladbach's sporting director in 2022?
questions.hint: Long-time academy chief Roland Virkus stepped up to replace Max Eberl after his resignation in early 2022.

questions.q: Which club did Denis Zakaria join when he left Gladbach in January 2022?
questions.hint: Zakaria moved to Juventus in the January 2022 window; his loan to Chelsea came the following summer.

questions.q: From which club did Gladbach sign long-time captain Lars Stindl in 2015?
questions.hint: Stindl arrived from Hannover 96 in 2015 and went on to captain Gladbach for years.

questions.q: Andreas Christensen spent two seasons on loan at Gladbach from 2015 to 2017 from which club?
questions.hint: The Danish defender was loaned to Gladbach by Chelsea for two seasons before returning to London.

questions.q: Which club did Eintracht Frankfurt beat in the 2022 Europa League final?
questions.hint: Frankfurt beat Rangers 5-4 on penalties in Seville after a 1-1 draw.

questions.q: Who was Eintracht Frankfurt's head coach when they won the 2021-22 Europa League?
questions.hint: Oliver Glasner led Frankfurt to the 2022 Europa League title in his first season in charge.

questions.q: Which club did Eintracht Frankfurt eliminate in the 2021-22 Europa League quarter-finals?
questions.hint: Frankfurt knocked out Barcelona, winning 3-2 at Camp Nou to go through 4-3 on aggregate.

questions.q: Which team did Eintracht Frankfurt beat 3-1 in the 2018 DFB-Pokal final?
questions.hint: Frankfurt upset Bayern Munich 3-1 in the 2018 final in Berlin.

questions.q: Who scored twice for Eintracht Frankfurt in the 2018 DFB-Pokal final?
questions.hint: Ante Rebić scored two goals in Frankfurt's 3-1 win over Bayern.

questions.q: Which coach won the 2018 DFB-Pokal with Eintracht Frankfurt before joining Bayern Munich?
questions.hint: Niko Kovač beat his future employer Bayern in the 2018 final, then took over at Bayern that summer.

questions.q: To which club did Eintracht Frankfurt sell Luka Jović in 2019?
questions.hint: Jović joined Real Madrid in the summer of 2019 after his breakout Frankfurt season.

questions.q: Which Premier League club signed Sébastien Haller from Eintracht Frankfurt in 2019?
questions.hint: Haller moved to West Ham United in 2019 for a then-club-record fee.

questions.q: Which Eintracht Frankfurt player finished as Bundesliga top scorer in 2014-15?
questions.hint: Alexander Meier, Frankfurt's 'Fußballgott', was the Bundesliga's top scorer in 2014-15 with 19 goals.

questions.q: Which club signed Randal Kolo Muani from Eintracht Frankfurt in 2023?
questions.hint: Kolo Muani joined Paris Saint-Germain on deadline day in the summer of 2023.

questions.q: From which club did Eintracht Frankfurt sign Randal Kolo Muani on a free transfer in 2022?
questions.hint: Kolo Muani arrived on a free transfer from Nantes in the summer of 2022.

questions.q: Which club signed Omar Marmoush from Eintracht Frankfurt in January 2025?
questions.hint: Marmoush joined Manchester City in the January 2025 transfer window.

questions.q: Which club knocked Eintracht Frankfurt out of the 2022-23 Champions League round of 16?
questions.hint: Napoli beat Frankfurt in both legs of the 2022-23 round of 16, winning 5-0 on aggregate.

questions.q: Who beat Eintracht Frankfurt in the 2023 DFB-Pokal final?
questions.hint: RB Leipzig won the 2023 final 2-0 against Frankfurt in Berlin.

questions.q: Which World Cup winner joined Eintracht Frankfurt from PSV Eindhoven in 2022?
questions.hint: Mario Götze, Germany's 2014 World Cup final goalscorer, signed from PSV in 2022.

questions.q: Which Serie A club signed Filip Kostić from Eintracht Frankfurt in 2022?
questions.hint: Kostić joined Juventus in August 2022, shortly after starring in Frankfurt's Europa League triumph.

questions.q: Who scored the only goal when Werder Bremen beat Bayer Leverkusen in the 2009 DFB-Pokal final?
questions.hint: Mesut Özil scored the winner in the 1-0 victory over Leverkusen in Berlin, sealing Werder's 2009 DFB-Pokal.

questions.q: Which club beat Werder Bremen in the 2009 UEFA Cup final?
questions.hint: Shakhtar Donetsk won the final 2-1 after extra time in Istanbul, the last edition before the Europa League rebrand.

questions.q: Which club did Miroslav Klose join when he left Werder Bremen in 2007?
questions.hint: Klose moved to Bayern Munich in 2007 after three seasons in Bremen; he only joined Lazio later, in 2011.

questions.q: From which club did Werder Bremen sign Mesut Özil in January 2008?
questions.hint: Özil arrived from Schalke 04 in the January 2008 window after falling out with the club, before starring for Werder.

questions.q: Which club signed Diego from Werder Bremen in the summer of 2009?
questions.hint: Juventus signed the Brazilian playmaker in 2009 after his three standout seasons in Bremen.

questions.q: Kevin De Bruyne spent the 2012-13 season on loan at Werder Bremen from which club?
questions.hint: De Bruyne was a Chelsea player at the time; his season-long loan in Bremen came years before his Manchester City move.

questions.q: Who was Werder Bremen's head coach continuously from 1999 until 2013?
questions.hint: Thomas Schaaf led Werder for 14 years from May 1999 to May 2013, including the 2004 double era.

questions.q: Which Werder Bremen player finished as the Bundesliga's joint top scorer in the 2022-23 season?
questions.hint: Niclas Füllkrug's 16 goals in 2022-23 made him joint top scorer alongside Leipzig's Christopher Nkunku.

questions.q: Which club did Niclas Füllkrug join when he left Werder Bremen in 2023?
questions.hint: Füllkrug moved to Borussia Dortmund late in the summer 2023 window; West Ham only signed him a year later.

questions.q: In which year were Werder Bremen relegated from the Bundesliga for the first time since 1980?
questions.hint: Werder went down in 2021 after finishing 17th in the 2020-21 season, ending four decades of unbroken top-flight football.

questions.q: Which club pipped Werder Bremen to the 2. Bundesliga title when both were promoted in 2022?
questions.hint: Schalke 04 won the 2021-22 second-division title with Werder promoted as runners-up; HSV missed out via the playoff.

questions.q: Who became Werder Bremen head coach in November 2021 and led them straight back to the Bundesliga?
questions.hint: Ole Werner took over in November 2021 after Markus Anfang resigned, and won promotion at the first attempt.

questions.q: Which Peruvian striker ended his playing career at Werder Bremen in 2020?
questions.hint: Club legend Claudio Pizarro retired at Werder in 2020 after his fourth spell with the club.

questions.q: From which club did Werder Bremen sign defender Per Mertesacker in 2006?
questions.hint: Mertesacker joined from his hometown club Hannover 96 in 2006 and stayed until his 2011 move to Arsenal.

questions.q: From which club did Werder Bremen sign Serge Gnabry in 2016?
questions.hint: Werder bought Gnabry from Arsenal in 2016; after one prolific season Bayern Munich snapped him up.

questions.q: Torsten Frings left Werder Bremen in 2011 to finish his career at which MLS club?
questions.hint: The long-time Werder captain joined Toronto FC in 2011 and played there until retiring.

questions.q: Which Borussia Mönchengladbach player won the 1977 Ballon d'Or?
questions.hint: Allan Simonsen won the 1977 Ballon d'Or after a season in which he scored in the European Cup final for Gladbach.

questions.q: Which English club beat Borussia Mönchengladbach 3-1 in the 1977 European Cup final in Rome?
questions.hint: Liverpool beat Gladbach 3-1 in Rome on 25 May 1977 to win their first European Cup.

questions.q: Gladbach won a Bundesliga match 12-0 in April 1978 — still the record league win. Who did they beat?
questions.hint: Borussia Dortmund lost 12-0 at Gladbach on 29 April 1978, which remains the biggest win in Bundesliga history.

questions.q: Who managed Borussia Mönchengladbach to their first Bundesliga title in 1970?
questions.hint: Hennes Weisweiler, in charge from 1964, delivered the club's first Bundesliga title in the 1969-70 season.

questions.q: Which Dutch club did Gladbach beat 5-1 in the second leg to win the 1975 UEFA Cup final?
questions.hint: After a 0-0 first leg, Gladbach won 5-1 away to FC Twente in Enschede to lift their first UEFA Cup in 1975.

questions.q: Which club did Gladbach overcome in the 1979 UEFA Cup final?
questions.hint: Gladbach beat Red Star Belgrade 2-1 on aggregate to win their second UEFA Cup in 1979.

questions.q: In the 1973 DFB-Pokal final, Günter Netzer subbed himself on and scored the winner against which club?
questions.hint: In his last game for Gladbach, Netzer brought himself on in extra time and scored the goal that beat 1. FC Köln 2-1.

questions.q: Which club did Günter Netzer join when he left Gladbach in the summer of 1973?
questions.hint: Günter Netzer left the Bökelberg for Real Madrid in 1973.

questions.q: Which stadium was Gladbach's home before the move to Borussia-Park in 2004?
questions.hint: Gladbach played their home matches at the Bökelbergstadion until Borussia-Park opened in 2004.

questions.q: Which club signed the young Lothar Matthäus from Gladbach in 1984?
questions.hint: Bayern Munich signed Lothar Matthäus from Gladbach in 1984, five years after his Gladbach debut.

questions.q: Gladbach beat which club 3-0 in the 1995 DFB-Pokal final?
questions.hint: Gladbach beat second-division VfL Wolfsburg 3-0 in Berlin to win the 1995 DFB-Pokal.

questions.q: In which year did Gladbach suffer their first-ever relegation from the Bundesliga?
questions.hint: Gladbach went down in 1999, their first relegation since joining the Bundesliga in 1965.

questions.q: Gladbach's fast, young, attacking side of the early 1970s earned which club nickname?
questions.hint: The young team was dubbed Die Fohlen — the Foals — a nickname the club still carries today.

questions.q: Why was Gladbach's 7-1 win over Inter Milan in the 1971 European Cup annulled?
o: Floodlight failure ended the match early
Gladbach had fielded an ineligible player
A can thrown from the crowd struck Inter's Roberto Boninsegna
A pitch invasion forced the referee to abandon play
questions.hint: A can thrown from the Bökelberg stands hit Inter striker Roberto Boninsegna, and UEFA annulled the 7-1 and ordered a replay.

questions.q: How many Bundesliga titles did Gladbach win during the 1970s?
questions.hint: Gladbach won five Bundesliga titles in the 1970s: 1970, 1971, 1975, 1976 and 1977.

questions.q: Who took over as Gladbach manager in 1975 when Hennes Weisweiler left for Barcelona?
questions.hint: Udo Lattek succeeded Weisweiler in 1975 and won two more Bundesliga titles plus the 1979 UEFA Cup.

questions.q: Which club did Eintracht Frankfurt beat 5-3 after extra time in the 1959 German championship final?
questions.hint: Eintracht beat local rivals Kickers Offenbach 5-3 after extra time in Berlin to win their first German title.

questions.q: Which club beat Eintracht Frankfurt 7-3 in the 1960 European Cup final at Hampden Park?
questions.hint: Real Madrid won 7-3 in Glasgow with four goals from Puskás and a Di Stéfano hat-trick.

questions.q: Which Scottish club did Frankfurt beat 6-1 and 6-3 in the 1960 European Cup semi-finals?
questions.hint: Frankfurt thrashed Rangers 6-1 at home and 6-3 in Glasgow to reach the 1960 final.

questions.q: Eintracht Frankfurt won the 1980 UEFA Cup on away goals against which fellow German club?
questions.hint: After a 3-2 away defeat, Frankfurt beat Borussia Mönchengladbach 1-0 at home to take the trophy on away goals.

questions.q: Which club did South Korean star Cha Bum-kun join when he left Eintracht Frankfurt in 1983?
questions.hint: Cha Bum-kun moved to Bayer Leverkusen in 1983 and later won a second UEFA Cup there in 1988.

questions.q: Which Eintracht Frankfurt player holds the record for most Bundesliga appearances, with 602?
questions.hint: Karl-Heinz Körbel made 602 Bundesliga appearances between 1972 and 1991, all for Eintracht — still the league record.

questions.q: Which Frankfurt player won the penalty that made it 1-1 for West Germany in the 1974 World Cup final?
questions.hint: Bernd Hölzenbein was brought down in the box, and Paul Breitner converted the equalising penalty.

questions.q: Who scored the free-kick winner when Frankfurt beat VfL Bochum in the 1988 DFB-Pokal final?
questions.hint: Lajos Détári curled an 81st-minute free-kick into the top corner for the 1-0 win over Bochum.

questions.q: Frankfurt lost the 1991-92 Bundesliga title race on the final day after defeat away to which club?
questions.hint: Frankfurt lost 2-1 at Hansa Rostock on the last day, and the title went to VfB Stuttgart instead.

questions.q: Who coached Eintracht Frankfurt during the dramatic 1991-92 Bundesliga title near-miss?
questions.hint: Dragoslav Stepanović led that side and coined the famous line 'Lebbe geht weider' after the final-day defeat.

questions.q: Which Eintracht Frankfurt striker finished as Bundesliga top scorer in both 1992-93 and 1993-94?
questions.hint: Anthony Yeboah topped the Bundesliga scoring charts in 1992-93 (shared with Ulf Kirsten) and again in 1993-94.

questions.q: Which Frankfurt midfielder scored a famous 1993 solo goal after twisting Oliver Kahn inside out?
questions.hint: Jay-Jay Okocha's dizzying dribble past Oliver Kahn against Karlsruhe in August 1993 became one of the Bundesliga's most replayed goals.

questions.q: Which club signed Jay-Jay Okocha from Eintracht Frankfurt in 1996?
questions.hint: Okocha joined Fenerbahçe in 1996, then moved on to Paris Saint-Germain two years later.

questions.q: Which English club signed striker Tony Yeboah from Eintracht Frankfurt in January 1995?
questions.hint: Yeboah joined Leeds United in January 1995 and became famous there for his thunderous volleys.

questions.q: Frankfurt escaped relegation on the 1999 final day with a stunning 5-1 win over which club?
questions.hint: Frankfurt beat 1. FC Kaiserslautern 5-1 on 29 May 1999, with Fjørtoft's late solo goal sealing survival.

questions.q: In which year were Eintracht Frankfurt relegated from the Bundesliga for the first time?
questions.hint: A founding Bundesliga member in 1963, Frankfurt went down for the first time in 1996.

questions.q: Which manager led Werder Bremen for 14 years from 1981, winning the Bundesliga in 1988 and 1993?
questions.hint: Otto Rehhagel managed Werder from 1981 to 1995, delivering the 1987-88 and 1992-93 Bundesliga titles in the club's golden era.

questions.q: Which club did Werder Bremen beat 2-0 in the 1992 European Cup Winners' Cup final?
questions.hint: Werder defeated AS Monaco 2-0 on 6 May 1992 to lift their first and only major European trophy.

questions.q: In which city was the 1992 European Cup Winners' Cup final, which Werder won, played?
questions.hint: The final was staged at the Estadio da Luz in Lisbon, in front of a famously sparse crowd of around 16,000.

questions.q: Who scored Werder's opening goal in the 1992 European Cup Winners' Cup final?
questions.hint: Klaus Allofs put Werder ahead before Wynton Rufer doubled the lead in the 2-0 win.

questions.q: Trailing 3-0 in a December 1993 Champions League group game, Werder came back to win 5-3 against whom?
questions.hint: The 5-3 comeback against RSC Anderlecht on 8 December 1993 became known as the 'Wunder von der Weser'.

questions.q: Werder won the 1999 DFB-Pokal final on penalties against which opponent?
questions.hint: Werder beat Bayern Munich 5-4 on penalties after a 1-1 draw in Berlin on 12 June 1999.

questions.q: Who took over as Werder Bremen head coach in May 1999 and later guided the club to the 2003-04 double?
questions.hint: Thomas Schaaf, a lifelong Werder man, was appointed in May 1999, won the cup within weeks and later delivered the 2004 double.

questions.q: Werder sealed the 2003-04 Bundesliga title with a 3-1 away win over which club?
questions.hint: Werder clinched the title on 8 May 2004 by winning 3-1 away at Bayern Munich with two games to spare.

questions.q: Which Werder player finished as the Bundesliga's top scorer in 2003-04 with 28 goals?
questions.hint: Brazilian striker Ailton hit 28 league goals in 2003-04, powering Werder to the double.

questions.q: Which Werder player in 2004 became the first non-German voted Germany's Footballer of the Year?
questions.hint: Ailton won the 2004 award after his 28-goal double season, the first foreign player ever to receive it.

questions.q: Which coach guided Werder Bremen to their first Bundesliga title in 1964-65?
questions.hint: Willi Multhaup's famously tight defence conceded just 29 goals as Werder won the 1964-65 championship.

questions.q: Which striker was the Bundesliga's top scorer in 1982-83 while playing for Werder Bremen?
questions.hint: Rudi Voller scored 23 league goals in 1982-83, his first Werder season, and was also named Footballer of the Year.

questions.q: Which country did Werder striker Wynton Rufer, a hero of the early-1990s side, play for internationally?
questions.hint: Wynton Rufer represented New Zealand, making him one of the Bundesliga's most celebrated Oceanian imports.

questions.q: From which club did Werder Bremen sign Miroslav Klose in 2004?
questions.hint: Klose moved to Werder from 1. FC Kaiserslautern in the summer of 2004.

questions.q: Which French playmaker ran the midfield in Werder's 2003-04 double-winning side?
questions.hint: Johan Micoud, signed from Parma in 2002, was the creative hub of the 2003-04 double team.

questions.q: Which Werder attacker spent his entire professional career, from 1989 to 2002, with the club?
questions.hint: Marco Bode played his whole professional career at Werder from 1989 until retiring in 2002, winning the league, cup and Cup Winners' Cup.

questions.q: Bologna beat which club in the 2025 Coppa Italia final?
questions.hint: Bologna beat AC Milan 1-0 at the Stadio Olimpico in Rome to lift the 2025 Coppa Italia.

questions.q: Who scored the only goal of the 2025 Coppa Italia final for Bologna?
questions.hint: Swiss winger Dan Ndoye struck the second-half winner in the 1-0 final victory.

questions.q: Who became Bologna's head coach in the summer of 2024?
questions.hint: Vincenzo Italiano took over from the departing Thiago Motta ahead of the 2024-25 season.

questions.q: Which club did Thiago Motta join as head coach after leaving Bologna in 2024?
questions.hint: Motta left Bologna to become Juventus head coach in the summer of 2024.

questions.q: Under Thiago Motta, in which position did Bologna finish in Serie A in 2023-24?
questions.hint: Bologna finished 5th in 2023-24, which was enough for Champions League qualification that year.

questions.q: Which club signed striker Joshua Zirkzee from Bologna in the summer of 2024?
questions.hint: Zirkzee joined Manchester United in the summer of 2024 after his breakout season at Bologna.

questions.q: Bologna signed defender Riccardo Calafiori in 2023 from which club?
questions.hint: Calafiori arrived from Swiss side Basel in 2023, a year before his big move to Arsenal.

questions.q: Bologna signed Marko Arnautovic in 2021 from which club?
questions.hint: Arnautovic returned to Europe from Chinese Super League side Shanghai Port in 2021.

questions.q: Bologna sold Japanese defender Takehiro Tomiyasu to which Premier League club in 2021?
questions.hint: Tomiyasu joined Arsenal on deadline day in the summer of 2021.

questions.q: Scottish midfielder Lewis Ferguson joined Bologna in 2022 from which club?
questions.hint: Ferguson moved to Bologna from Aberdeen in 2022 and later captained the side.

questions.q: Which former Serbia international coached Bologna from 2019 until 2022?
questions.hint: Sinisa Mihajlovic led Bologna from January 2019 to September 2022, continuing to coach during his leukemia treatment.

questions.q: Bologna president Joey Saputo is also the owner of which North American soccer club?
questions.hint: Saputo owns CF Montreal (formerly the Montreal Impact); his family took control of Bologna in 2014.

questions.q: Bologna returned to Serie A in 2015 after beating which club in the Serie B playoff final?
questions.hint: Bologna overcame Pescara in the 2015 Serie B promotion playoff final to go straight back up.

questions.q: Which Premier League club signed full-back Aaron Hickey from Bologna in 2022?
questions.hint: The Scottish full-back joined Brentford in the summer of 2022.

questions.q: Winger Riccardo Orsolini arrived at Bologna in 2018 from which club?
questions.hint: Orsolini joined Bologna from Juventus in January 2018, initially on loan before the move was made permanent.

questions.q: Bologna signed goalkeeper Lukasz Skorupski in 2018 from which club?
questions.hint: Skorupski joined from Roma in 2018 and became Bologna's first-choice goalkeeper.

questions.q: Bologna sealed the 1963-64 Serie A title by winning a playoff in Rome against which club?
questions.hint: Bologna beat Inter Milan 2-0 in the title playoff at Rome's Stadio Olimpico in June 1964.

questions.q: Who was Bologna's head coach for their 1963-64 Serie A title win?
questions.hint: Fulvio Bernardini managed the side that won Bologna's seventh and most recent scudetto.

questions.q: Which Bologna player finished as Serie A's top scorer in both 1962-63 and 1963-64?
questions.hint: Danish striker Harald Nielsen won back-to-back capocannoniere titles in those two seasons.

questions.q: Which Bologna forward scored in each of the club's first 10 Serie A games of 1962-63?
questions.hint: Ezio Pascutti's 10-match scoring streak stood until Gabriel Batistuta surpassed it in 1994-95.

questions.q: Who holds Bologna's all-time appearance record, spending his entire career (1959-75) at the club?
questions.hint: Giacomo Bulgarelli, Bologna's iconic captain, made more appearances than anyone in club history.

questions.q: Bologna won the 1974 Coppa Italia final on penalties against which club?
questions.hint: Bologna edged Serie B side Palermo in a shoot-out after a draw to lift the 1974 Coppa Italia.

questions.q: Renato Dall'Ara, after whom Bologna's stadium was renamed in 1983, served the club as what?
questions.hint: Dall'Ara was Bologna's long-serving president, dying just days before the 1964 title playoff.

questions.q: Which Italian forward struck a personal-best 22 Serie A goals for Bologna in 1997-98?
questions.hint: Roberto Baggio's 22 goals in his single Bologna season earned him a place at the 1998 World Cup.

questions.q: Which former Lazio striker joined Bologna in late 1998 and stayed until 2004?
questions.hint: Giuseppe Signori moved to Bologna in November 1998 and became a club favourite.

questions.q: Bologna won the 1998 UEFA Intertoto Cup by beating which side in the final?
questions.hint: Bologna beat Ruch Chorzow over two legs; Valencia and Werder Bremen won the other 1998 finals.

questions.q: Bologna's 1998-99 UEFA Cup run ended in the semi-finals against which club?
questions.hint: Marseille edged Bologna in the semi-final before losing the final to Parma.

questions.q: Which coach took Bologna from Serie C1 back to Serie A with straight promotions in 1995 and 1996?
questions.hint: Renzo Ulivieri led Bologna to back-to-back promotions and their 1996 return to Serie A.

questions.q: Which German international played in Bologna's 1963-64 title-winning side?
questions.hint: Helmut Haller starred for Bologna from 1962 to 1968, including the 1964 scudetto season.

questions.q: Which Italy goalkeeper joined Bologna from Inter in 1999?
questions.hint: Gianluca Pagliuca signed from Inter in 1999 and kept goal for Bologna until 2006.

questions.q: Bologna went down from Serie A in 2005 after losing a relegation playoff to which club?
questions.hint: Parma won the two-legged spareggio in June 2005, sending Bologna down to Serie B.

questions.q: Which Swedish striker from the 1994 World Cup bronze side led Bologna's attack in the late 1990s?
questions.hint: Kennet Andersson spearheaded Bologna's attack, including the 1998-99 UEFA Cup semi-final run.

questions.q: In the 1992 UEFA Cup quarter-finals, Genoa became the first Italian side to win at which English stadium?
questions.hint: Genoa beat Liverpool 2-1 at Anfield in April 1992, the first win there by any Italian club.

questions.q: Which club knocked Genoa out of the 1991-92 UEFA Cup at the semi-final stage?
questions.hint: Ajax edged Genoa in the semi-final and went on to lift that season's UEFA Cup.

questions.q: Who coached Genoa to fourth place in Serie A and UEFA Cup qualification in 1990-91?
questions.hint: Osvaldo Bagnoli guided Genoa to fourth in 1990-91, the finish that launched the famous UEFA Cup run.

questions.q: Tomáš Skuhravý joined Genoa after scoring five goals at Italia '90 — for which national team?
questions.hint: Skuhravý's five goals for Czechoslovakia at the 1990 World Cup earned him his move to Genoa.

questions.q: Which Uruguayan forward struck up Genoa's famous early-1990s attacking partnership with Tomáš Skuhravý?
questions.hint: Carlos Aguilera partnered Skuhravý up front, and his brace won the 1992 UEFA Cup tie at Anfield.

questions.q: Genoa went down from Serie A in 1995 after losing a relegation playoff on penalties to which club?
questions.hint: Padova beat Genoa on penalties in the June 1995 relegation playoff in Florence after a 1-1 draw.

questions.q: Genoa lifted the 1996 Anglo-Italian Cup at Wembley by beating which English club in the final?
questions.hint: Genoa beat Port Vale 5-2 at Wembley to win the 1996 Anglo-Italian Cup.

questions.q: Which Japanese forward joined Genoa in 1994, becoming the first Japanese player to appear in Serie A?
questions.hint: Kazuyoshi Miura spent 1994-95 at Genoa as Serie A's first Japanese player, and scored in the derby against Sampdoria.

questions.q: After a prolific 1995-96 Serie B season with Genoa, striker Vincenzo Montella moved to which club?
questions.hint: Montella crossed the Derby della Lanterna divide, joining city rivals Sampdoria in 1996.

questions.q: Genoa retired which shirt number in memory of captain Gianluca Signorini after his death in 2002?
questions.hint: Genoa retired the No. 6 in honour of Gianluca Signorini, their UEFA Cup-run captain, who died of ALS in 2002.

questions.q: Franco Scoglio, who took Genoa back to Serie A as 1988-89 Serie B champions, went by which nickname?
questions.hint: Scoglio was known as 'Il Professore' — the Professor — during his celebrated spells on the Genoa bench.

questions.q: Genoa finished top of Serie B in 2004-05, but a match-fixing verdict sent them down to which division?
questions.hint: The 'Caso Genoa' verdict over the Genoa-Venezia match saw the club demoted to Serie C1 instead of promoted.

questions.q: Which Argentine striker led Genoa's attack in the 2004-05 Serie B campaign?
questions.hint: Diego Milito's goals powered Genoa's 2004-05 Serie B campaign during his first spell at the club.

questions.q: Which businessman took control of Genoa in 2003, beginning a long reign as club president?
questions.hint: Toy magnate Enrico Preziosi bought Genoa in 2003 and remained president for nearly two decades.

questions.q: Genoa's Stadio Luigi Ferraris was rebuilt into its current form as a venue for which tournament?
questions.hint: The Marassi was completely rebuilt in the late 1980s to host matches at the 1990 World Cup.

questions.q: Roberto Pruzzo, Genoa's homegrown goalscoring hero of the 1970s, was sold in 1978 to which club?
questions.hint: Genoa sold Pruzzo to Roma in 1978, where he went on to win the Serie A top-scorer crown three times.

questions.q: Who was Lille's head coach when they won the 2020-21 Ligue 1 title?
questions.hint: Christophe Galtier led Lille to the 2020-21 title, then left for Nice that summer.

questions.q: By how many points did Lille finish above PSG when they won Ligue 1 in 2020-21?
questions.hint: Lille finished on 83 points to PSG's 82 — a margin of one point, sealed on the final day at Angers.

questions.q: Which club signed Eden Hazard from Lille in the summer of 2012?
questions.hint: Chelsea signed Hazard from Lille in June 2012; he only joined Real Madrid seven years later.

questions.q: Which club paid a then club-record fee to sign Nicolas Pepe from Lille in 2019?
questions.hint: Arsenal made Pepe their record signing at around 72 million pounds in the summer of 2019.

questions.q: Which club did Victor Osimhen join when he left Lille in 2020?
questions.hint: Napoli signed Osimhen from Lille in the summer of 2020 for a fee reported above 70 million euros.

questions.q: Who was Lille's first-choice goalkeeper during the 2020-21 title-winning season?
questions.hint: Mike Maignan kept goal throughout the 2020-21 title season before joining AC Milan in 2021.

questions.q: From which club did Lille sign veteran striker Burak Yilmaz in 2020?
questions.hint: Yilmaz arrived from Besiktas in August 2020 and became a talisman of the title-winning side.

questions.q: Who scored a hat-trick in Lille's 3-0 Europa League win away at AC Milan in November 2020?
questions.hint: Yusuf Yazici scored all three at San Siro on 5 November 2020, ending Milan's long unbeaten run.

questions.q: Who managed Lille to the Ligue 1 and Coupe de France double in 2010-11?
questions.hint: Rudi Garcia coached Lille to the 2010-11 double, the club's first league title since 1954.

questions.q: Which Lille player finished as Ligue 1's top scorer in the 2010-11 double season?
questions.hint: Moussa Sow topped the 2010-11 Ligue 1 scoring charts with 25 goals for Lille.

questions.q: Which club signed Dutch centre-back Sven Botman from Lille in 2022?
questions.hint: Newcastle United signed Botman in the summer of 2022 after AC Milan had long been linked.

questions.q: Which stadium has been Lille's home ground since 2012?
questions.hint: Lille moved into the ground now called Stade Pierre-Mauroy in 2012, leaving Stadium Lille Metropole.

questions.q: Which club signed teenage defender Leny Yoro from Lille in 2024?
questions.hint: Manchester United signed Yoro in July 2024, beating long-time suitors Real Madrid to the deal.

questions.q: Who scored the winning penalty when Lille beat Real Madrid 1-0 in the Champions League in October 2024?
questions.hint: Jonathan David converted a first-half stoppage-time penalty on 2 October 2024 to sink the holders.

questions.q: From which club did Lille sign Renato Sanches in 2019?
questions.hint: Lille bought Sanches from Bayern Munich in August 2019; he joined PSG only after the Lille title.

questions.q: Which club did Lille beat 1-0 to win the 2021 Trophee des Champions?
questions.hint: Lille beat Paris Saint-Germain 1-0 in the August 2021 Trophee des Champions, with Xeka scoring.

questions.q: In which year did Lille win the French top-flight title for the second and final time in the 20th century?
questions.hint: Lille won the 1953-54 Division 1 championship — 1954, their second title after 1946 and their last until 2011.

questions.q: Which club did Lille beat 5-2 in the 1955 Coupe de France final?
questions.hint: Lille thrashed Bordeaux 5-2 at Colombes, with goals from Jean Vincent, Yvon Douis (2) and Gerard Bourbotte (2).

questions.q: Who did Lille defeat 2-1 in the 1953 Coupe de France final?
questions.hint: Jean Vincent and Bernard Lefevre scored as Lille beat FC Nancy 2-1 at Colombes.

questions.q: Which France international won a league title and two Coupes de France with Lille before joining Reims in 1956?
questions.hint: Winger Jean Vincent won the 1954 championship and the 1953 and 1955 cups at Lille, then moved to Reims in 1956.

questions.q: Which manager, appointed in 1998, took Lille from Division 2 back to the French top flight?
questions.hint: Vahid Halilhodzic, hired in October 1998, won the 1999-2000 Division 2 title by a wide margin to seal promotion.

questions.q: Lille won the 1999-2000 Division 2 title. In which year had they been relegated from the top flight?
questions.hint: A financial crisis sent Lille down at the end of the 1996-97 season — relegated in 1997, back up in 2000.

questions.q: Which Italian club did Lille eliminate in the 2001-02 Champions League third qualifying round?
questions.hint: Lille won 2-0 in Parma and went through 2-1 on aggregate to reach their first Champions League group stage.

questions.q: Manchester United and Olympiacos were in Lille's 2001-02 Champions League group. Which Spanish club completed it?
questions.hint: Group G paired Lille with Manchester United, Olympiacos and Deportivo La Coruna.

questions.q: Which French midfielder did Liverpool sign from Lille in the summer of 2002?
questions.hint: Bruno Cheyrou joined Liverpool for around 4.5 million pounds, famously hailed as 'the new Zidane' by Gerard Houllier.

questions.q: Arsenal paid around 2 million pounds in 2002 to sign which centre-back from Lille?
questions.hint: Pascal Cygan joined Arsenal for 2.1 million pounds and featured in the 2003-04 title-winning squad.

questions.q: Who was appointed Lille head coach in July 2002, beginning a six-year spell at the club?
questions.hint: Claude Puel arrived in July 2002 and stayed until 2008, when he left for Lyon.

questions.q: Lille finished runners-up in Ligue 1 in 2004-05. Which club won the title that season?
questions.hint: Lyon took a fourth consecutive championship, finishing 12 points clear of second-placed Lille.

questions.q: Lille won the 2004 UEFA Intertoto Cup by beating which Portuguese club in the final?
questions.hint: Lille beat Uniao de Leiria 2-0 on aggregate, with extra-time goals from Moussilou and Acimovic in the second leg.

questions.q: Which stadium did Lille leave in 2004 after nearly three decades as their home ground?
questions.hint: Stade Grimonprez-Jooris, Lille's home since 1975, hosted its last match in May 2004 before the move to Stadium Lille-Metropole.

questions.q: Which future France goalkeeper started his professional career at Lille in 1981?
questions.hint: Bernard Lama spent 1981-1989 at Lille before going on to Lens, PSG and the France national team.
